subtitle: How Bhoja Turned Stone, Verse, and City into One Science

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a half-built great temple and city plan etched on the ground, Bhoja at the center with palm-leaf manuscript and measuring cord
panels.action: Bhoja of Dhara stands on a rocky rise above the Narmada plain, one hand on a vast ground-drawing of a temple plan at Bhojpur, the other holding a thick palm-leaf manuscript as artisans and architects work below.

dialogue.text: In Bhoja’s Malwa, a king’s court set out to bind earth, temple and machine into one science—the seven thousand verses of the Samarangana Sutradhara.

i18n.hi: भोज के मालवा में, एक राजदरबार ने धरती, मंदिर और मशीन को एक ही विद्या में बाँधने की ठानी—समरांगण सूत्रधार के सात हज़ार श्लोकों में।

panels.shot: slow push-in from bird’s-eye of Malwa plateau to close view of Dhara’s palace complex
panels.action: A broad view of the Malwa plateau shows Dhara’s palace rising amid clustered houses and temples, with roads radiating outward; in a balcony, Bhoja leans over a railing, watching the busy city below.

dialogue.text: Dhara, early eleventh century. Under Bhoja’s gaze, Malwa’s capital swells with streets, shrines and markets—its growth no longer a jumble, but a question: can a city be written like a book?

i18n.hi: धारा, ग्यारहवीं सदी की शुरुआत। भोज की नज़र में मालवा की राजधानी गलियों, मंदिरों और बाज़ारों से फूल उठी—अब बिखराव नहीं, सवाल ये कि क्या शहर को किताब की तरह लिखा जा सकता है?

panels.shot: medium close-up of Bhoja seated in a council hall, scrolls and treatises spread before him
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, Bhoja sits cross-legged amid stacks of palm-leaf manuscripts, while scribes kneel nearby; he studies a leaf inscribed in fine Nagari script, his brow furrowed in thought.

dialogue.text: Earlier masters had spoken of houses and temples in scattered sutras, guild rules and regional memory. Bhoja’s court turned these streams toward one aim: a complete science of building.

i18n.hi: पहले आचार्यों ने घर और मंदिर पर बिखरे सूत्रों, गिल्ड नियमों और प्रादेशिक स्मृति में कहा था। भोज के दरबार ने इन धाराओं को एक लक्ष्य पर मोड़ा: निर्माण की संपूर्ण विद्या।

panels.shot: low, intimate shot of Bhoja dictating to scribes in lamplight
panels.action: By lamplight, Bhoja gestures with a stylus as two scribes sit before him, writing on fresh palm leaves; behind them, a faint outline of a temple plan is traced on a board.

dialogue.text: The treatise that emerged, later called Samarangana Sutradhara, bears Bhoja’s name. Whether from his own hand or his court’s, its voice is royal: it speaks as if a king instructs the master-builder.

i18n.hi: जो ग्रंथ बना, आगे चलकर समरांगण सूत्रधार कहलाया, वो भोज के नाम से जुड़ा। भले हाथ किसी का हो, आवाज़ शाही है—जैसे राजा खुद शिल्पाचार्य को दिशा दे रहा हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of open ground outside Dhara with Bhoja and architects testing soil
panels.action: On an open field, Bhoja stands with architects and craftsmen as they dig test pits, knead soil in their fingers, and pour water into a shallow trench to watch it drain.

dialogue.text: The text begins at the ground itself: how to choose land, test soil by sight, smell and touch, judge wind, water and slope—before a single brick is laid.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ ज़मीन से शुरू होता है: धरती चुनना, मिट्टी को देखने, सूँघने, छूने से परखना, हवा, पानी और ढाल को तौलना—पहला ईंट भी रखने से पहले।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of a city plan traced with cords and pegs on the earth
panels.action: Ropes, pegs and chalk mark a rectilinear grid on packed earth; Bhoja and surveyors stride along lines that suggest streets, wards and a central temple square taking shape.

dialogue.text: Then come towns and forts: grids and mandalas of streets, wards for traders and artisans, placements for markets, wells and temples. A city is drawn first on earth, then raised in stone.

i18n.hi: फिर आते हैं नगर और दुर्ग: गलियों के ग्रिड और मंडल, बनियों और कारीगरों के मुहल्ले, बाज़ार, कुओं और मंदिरों की जगेह। शहर पहले धरती पर खिंचता, फिर पत्थर में उठता है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a partially finished house, carpenters and masons at work
panels.action: In a half-built courtyard house, carpenters fit wooden beams while masons lay stone courses; Bhoja observes, pointing out the alignment of door, window and courtyard.

dialogue.text: Domestic life, too, is measured: house types for rich and poor, room proportions, courtyards for light and air, thresholds and doorways aligned not by whim, but by rule.

i18n.hi: घरेलू जीवन भी नापा गया: अमीर-गरीब के घरों के प्रकार, कमरों के अनुपात, रोशनी और हवा के लिए आँगन, चौखट और दरवाज़े मनमर्ज़ी से नहीं, नियम से जमे।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of Bhojpur riverside with massive platform and unfinished lingam, plans etched nearby
panels.action: On the rocky bank at Bhojpur, a colossal stone platform and a towering unfinished linga rise; beside them, intricate ground-lines and carving marks map out a great temple that was never fully built.

dialogue.text: At Bhojpur, near the Betwa, time preserves a rare echo: the ground-drawings and unfinished mass of a colossal temple, where theory and experiment met under Bhoja’s rule.

i18n.hi: बेतवा किनारे भोजपुर में, समय ने एक अनोखी गूँज सँभाल रखी है: ज़मीन पर खींची रेखाएँ और अधूरा विराट मंदिर, जहाँ सिद्धांत और प्रयोग भोज के राज में मिले।

panels.shot: top-down close-up of carved planning lines on Bhojpur stones with Bhoja’s hand hovering above
panels.action: A close view shows fine incised grids and curves on a stone slab at Bhojpur, Bhoja’s hand hovering above as if matching them to a palm-leaf leaf in his other hand.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars trace these lines and compare them with the Samarangana’s verses on temple plans and superstructures, seeing in Bhojpur an open page of stone beside a page of verse.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान इन रेखाओं को पढ़ते हैं और समरांगण के मंदिर-योजना और ऊर्ध्वभाग के श्लोकों से मिलाते हैं, भोजपुर को पत्थर का खुला पृष्ठ और श्लोकों का पृष्ठ साथ-साथ देखते हैं।

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle shot of a Bhumija-type temple shikhara rising against the sky
panels.action: A soaring temple tower of the bhumija type rises in tiers of miniature spires, each offset in a lattice-like pattern, while Bhoja looks up from the base, the complex geometry reflected in his eyes.

dialogue.text: The text’s temple chapters dwell on soaring shikharas, including the bhumija form—lattices of miniature spires—which later Malwa temples would turn into stone diagrams of rhythm and repetition.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ के मंदिर-अध्याय ऊँचे शिखरों पर ठहरते हैं, खासकर भूमिज रूप पर—छोटे शिखरों की जालियाँ—जिन्हें बाद के मालवा मंदिरों ने लय और पुनरावृत्ति के पत्थर-चित्र बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a sculptor’s workshop with images in different stages
panels.action: Inside a shady workshop, sculptors chip away at blocks that become deities, dancers and guardians; Bhoja stands amid them, indicating with his hand the posture of a figure.

dialogue.text: Beyond plans and walls, the Samarangana speaks of images and icons: measures for limbs, poses and expressions, so that the deity’s presence, the dancer’s grace, follow a shared canon.

i18n.hi: योजना और दीवारों से आगे, समरांगण मूर्तियों की भी बात करता है: अंगों के माप, भंगिमाएँ और भाव, ताकि देवता की उपस्थिति, नर्तकी की लय, एक ही विधान में बँधे।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of painters at work on a shrine wall
panels.action: Painters kneel before a plastered shrine wall, grinding pigments and tracing outlines, as Bhoja watches and gestures toward the arrangement of figures and motifs.

dialogue.text: Painting and ornament, too, find place: how to lay out panels on walls, how colors and motifs should support the shrine’s form, so that structure and image speak one language.

i18n.hi: चित्र और अलंकरण को भी जगह मिलती है: दीवारों पर पैनल कैसे बाँटें, रंग और आकृतियाँ कैसे गर्भगृह के रूप को साधें, ताकि ढांचा और छवि एक ही भाषा बोलें।

panels.shot: low-lit, focused shot of Bhoja and craftsmen examining a mechanical device without revealing details
panels.action: In a dim chamber, Bhoja and a circle of craftsmen bend over a wooden frame with gears and levers, its exact form obscured in shadow, as a small figure carved in wood stands nearby.

dialogue.text: In later chapters, the text turns to yantras—mechanical contrivances, even devices said to fly. Yet it withholds full instruction, hinting at marvels while guarding their working.

i18n.hi: आगे के अध्याय यंत्रों पर मुड़ते हैं—यांत्रिक करामातें, यहाँ तक कि उड़ने कहे गए उपकरण। पर ग्रंथ पूरा ब्योरा रोक लेता है, अद्भुत की झलक देता है, काम की गाँठ छुपाए रखता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bhoja dismissing a courtier excitedly gesturing upwards
panels.action: A courtier looks up and gestures skyward as if imagining flight, while Bhoja, calm, lowers his hand in a restraining gesture, a faint smile acknowledging the idea without exaggeration.

dialogue.text: Later ages would weave legends of Bhoja’s flying machines. The text itself, and the earth at Bhojpur, stay silent on such claims, speaking instead of measured craft and controlled wonder.

i18n.hi: आने वाली सदियों ने भोज के उड़ने वाले यंत्रों की कथाएँ बुनीं। पर ग्रंथ खुद, और भोजपुर की धरती, इन दावों पर चुप रहते हैं—वे बस नपी-तुली कारीगरी और सँयमी चमत्कार की बात करते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bhoja teaching architects in a hall, with diagrams and models around
panels.action: In a spacious hall, Bhoja addresses a gathered circle of sthapatis and artisans, around them small models of temples, house layouts drawn on boards, and carved capitals resting on the floor.

dialogue.text: For Bhoja’s court, architecture was not just craft but shastra—rule and reasoning, passed in sutras, tested in stone, and taught to those who would raise the next generation of cities and shrines.

i18n.hi: भोज के दरबार में वास्तु सिर्फ हुनर नहीं, शास्त्र था—नियम और तर्क, जो सूत्रों में दिया गया, पत्थर में परखा गया, और उन्हें सिखाया गया जो अगली पीढ़ी के नगर और मंदिर उठाएँगे।

panels.shot: dissolve-style composition showing a palm-leaf of Samarangana beside a later Aparajitaprccha manuscript
panels.action: A close view juxtaposes an older palm-leaf manuscript labeled by style as Samarangana Sutradhara with a slightly later one in similar script echoing its lines, as a ghosted profile of Bhoja looks on.

dialogue.text: A century later, the Aparajitaprccha would cite the Samarangana as authority. Bhoja’s courtly compilation, once royal instruction, had become a reference for distant builders.

i18n.hi: एक सदी बाद, अपराजितपृच्छा ने समरांगण को प्रमाण माना। भोज का दरबारी संकलन, जो कभी राजाज्ञा था, दूर-दराज़ के शिल्पियों के लिए संदर्भ बन गया।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Bhoja at Bhojpur to a montage of many temples and towns across Malwa
panels.action: Standing again at Bhojpur, Bhoja looks over the unfinished temple; as the view pulls back, silhouettes of later Malwa temples and townscapes appear around him like echoes across the landscape.

dialogue.text: Today, scholars walk Bhojpur’s plans and Malwa’s bhumija towers with the Samarangana in hand, tracing how verses shaped stone, and how a king’s curiosity met the test of the world.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान भोजपुर की रेखाएँ और मालवा के भूमिज शिखर समरांगण हाथ में लेकर नापते हैं, देखते हैं कैसे श्लोकों ने पत्थर को गढ़ा, और कैसे एक राजा की जिज्ञासा दुनिया की कसौटी पर खरी उतरी।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Bhoja’s thoughtful face, city and temple blurred behind
panels.action: Bhoja’s face fills the frame, eyes distant and reflective, while behind him, blurred, lie hints of city streets, a temple silhouette and a craftsman’s tools.

dialogue.text: In Bhoja’s age, knowledge proved itself not in boasts but in buildings. His seven thousand verses endure where they were tested—in foundations that still hold, and forms that still rise against the sky.

i18n.hi: भोज के समय में ज्ञान शेख़ी से नहीं, इमारतों से साबित होता था। उसके सात हज़ार श्लोक वहीं टिके हैं जहाँ परखे गए थे—उन नींवों में जो आज भी थामे हैं, और उन रूपों में जो आज भी आसमान को छूते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Seven Thousand Verses for a City
title_i18n.hi: एक शहर के लिए सात हज़ार श्लोक

subtitle_i18n.en: How Bhoja Turned Stone, Verse, and City into One Science
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे भोज ने पत्थर, श्लोक और शहर को एक ही विद्या बना दिया
